questions.q: What does the acronym CRUD stand for in Salesforce object permissions?
options: Create, Read, Update, Disable
Create, Read, Edit, Delete
Control, Restrict, Use, Delete
Clone, Read, Edit, Duplicate
questions.explain: CRUD is Create, Read, Edit, Delete — the four base object permissions.

questions.q: A user has Read and Edit on Opportunity but not Create or Delete. Per this lesson, is that a valid configuration?
options: No, CRUD permissions must always be granted or revoked together
No, Edit requires Create to also be enabled
Yes, each CRUD permission is independent of the others
Yes, but only on custom objects, never standard ones
questions.explain: The lesson states each CRUD permission is independent — Read+Edit without Create/Delete is a common, valid setup.

questions.q: What makes View All and Modify All different from the four base CRUD permissions?
options: They only apply to custom objects
They are assigned through roles instead of profiles
They bypass record-level sharing entirely rather than working within it
They require a separate Salesforce license
questions.explain: View All and Modify All are administrative overrides that bypass the entire record-level access system, unlike the base four.

questions.q: Where do object permissions (CRUD) actually live in Salesforce, per this lesson?
options: On roles in the role hierarchy
On profiles and permission sets
On organization-wide default settings
On individual records directly
questions.explain: The lesson states object permissions are never stored on a role — they live on profiles and permission sets.

questions.q: Since Winter '21, what changed about CRUD on standard objects for standard profiles?
options: It was removed from Salesforce entirely
It became editable only through Apex code
Editing it was disabled -- only custom profiles let an admin edit those attributes
It now requires View All to be enabled first
questions.explain: The guide notes that editing standard objects on standard profiles has been disabled since Winter '21; custom profiles remain editable.
